newsitem.title: UK: Volatile LME copper bid lower in evening session.
newsitem.headline: Volatile LME copper bid lower in evening session.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper was bid lower during Friday's evening session after an alarmingly volatile kerb trade that saw prices tumbling from highs at the close.
Three-month copper was indicated at $2,365 a tonne at 1910 GMT, down $25 on the kerb close, after having dipped to $2,360 in the evening trade.

During the kerb, copper lost all the gains racked up and pulled most other metals back. Traders said it came under heavy pressure from liquidation and end-week sales after a midsession upside break was not sustained.
From a fresh nine-month high of $2,445 a tonne, the market tumbled back to close Friday's kerb at $2,390, a $13 loss from yesterday.

"The close is disappointing and with the technical indicators turning down, we feel that further weakness can be expected...these current high prices should be viewed as selling opportunities...," said Rudolf Wolff in a daily commentary.
But despite the slide, most traders remain bullish on copper, given continued stock falls.
Aluminium was indicated at $1,673 after ending the kerb at $1,675, down $14.
